opening:
We thank the Editor in Chief, the Associate Editor and the three reviewers for a careful and
constructive reading. The reviews sent us back to the code, and we want to report at the outset what
we found there, because it changed the revision substantially and it is the honest starting point for
everything that follows.

Reviewer 1 comment 4 asks why the fuzzy rule weights 1.5 and 2.0 were chosen. Reviewer 3 comment 17
asks how the parameters of the fuzzy layer were computed. Reviewer 3 comment 13 asks us to release
the code. Answering the first two properly meant instrumenting the rule layer, and doing that
revealed a defect. In the submitted version the allocation map produced by the symbolic negotiator
was the constant one at every pixel of every image. The positive rule contributions summed to more
than the upper limit of the clamp that follows them, so the clamp was active everywhere. Because the
derivative of a clamp at its bound is zero, the rule parameters also received no gradient during
training and remained at their initial values. We verified both facts directly, first by reading the
allocation map out of the released checkpoint, and second by confirming that every negotiator
parameter in that checkpoint is still exactly at its initializer after 2082 optimizer steps.

The consequence is that the symbolic layer described in Section III of the submitted paper did not
influence any reported number. We are grateful that the reviewers pushed on exactly this point.

We have repaired the method rather than removed the claim. The allocation is now a bounded weighted
vote over the five named rules, with budgets chosen so that the value provably lies in the unit
interval for every possible input and every possible parameter setting. The clamp is therefore never
active, saturation is impossible rather than merely unlikely, and gradients reach the rule parameters
again. The repair also strengthens the theory. The Lipschitz constant of the allocation is now exact
and attained rather than a loose upper bound, it can be computed from the trained weights, and
Section V reports the realized ratio measured against it on real images.

Instrumenting the code for the release exposed five further defects in how the submitted models
were trained and selected, and we list them here rather than in the individual answers. First, ten
loss weight flags of the training script were parsed and never passed to the loss, so the four
settings of the earlier search differed in the fidelity dead zone alone, and the description of
parameter selection in the submitted paper was wrong about what had been selected. Second, nothing
was seeded, and the selector chose a setting on one run and then reported a fresh unseeded model
trained with that setting and a different batch size, so the reported model was never the selected
model. Third, the DnCNN backbone contains batch normalization and its running statistics kept
updating while it served as the frozen reference, so the reference drifted during training. Fourth,
the SwinIR corrector was trained against a half resolution cache of the backbone output and tested
against the full resolution output, which differ by 1.61 dB. Fifth, on a graphics processor the
script compiled the corrector for training while every scoring script ran it eagerly, which moved the
frozen reference of DnCNN and SwinIR by about a sixth of the size of the correction itself. All five
are fixed. Every source of
randomness is now seeded, every setting is trained at three seeds and selected on its worst seed,
the normalization statistics are held fixed, the cache runs at full resolution, compilation is
disabled on every path, and the search varies exactly the two quantities that act. The released code documents each defect and includes a
script that checks each fix.

Every model was retrained from the submitted checkpoints with the repaired method and every table
was regenerated from the selected seeded checkpoints. The original
behavior remains reproducible through a documented switch, so the numbers in the submitted version
can still be recovered from the released code.

Discrepancies between the submitted text and the code were found in the same pass and are corrected
in the revision. The blend weight at test time is one when at least two of the three safety
constraints hold, rather than the four valued schedule printed in the submitted Equation 16. The
cross dataset protocol involved per fold adaptation on the target dataset, which is precisely what
Reviewer 2 comment 1 identified, and the revision now reports transfer with no adaptation as the
only protocol of the main paper. Reading the objective line by line against the code found three
more. The clinical term is a weighted one sided penalty against a target taken from the backbone, over
nine quantities and not a sum of two log ratios, and the tissue contrast index is not among the nine.
The edge term is weighted toward the edges of the clean reference and carries two further parts. A
sixth term of bounds and background protection, eight penalties in all, was active in training and
absent from the printed objective. All of them now appear with their constants in Equations 14 to 19,
and the property term was corrected in the same way.

The manuscript has been rewritten rather than patched. It is now organized from the top down, every
symbol is defined before it is used, and the wording avoids the em dash, the colon and the semicolon
throughout at the request of our own readability review. Point by point answers follow.
summary: Repaired the allocation rule so the symbolic layer actually acts, fixed five further defects in training and selection, retrained every model at three seeds from the submitted checkpoints, and regenerated every table. The Lipschitz result is now exact, attained, and verified numerically.

Restated the cross dataset protocol. The main paper now reports transfer with no adaptation of any kind and nothing else. The adapted protocol of the original submission keeps, in each fold, the epoch that scores best on the subject that fold then reports, so it is reported only in the supplementary file and labeled a historical diagnostic.
Added a leave one property out study over all six clinical properties on the full test set.
Added a sensitivity study over the constants of the rule layer, including two alternative conjunctions.
Added a comparison against a plain corrector of the same size trained with the same objective, and against two classical post processing operators.
Added a direct test of whether the confidence map predicts backbone error.
Added a safety analysis that measures invented edges, retention of weak structures, behavior inside dark fluid like regions, and worst case per image change.
Added a numerical check of both theorems and of how often each safety constraint binds.
Added a new section that states the optimization problem, its variables, its constraints and its solver, and a notation table that defines every symbol before first use.
Rewrote the paper from the top down, renamed all uses of the word experiment to test or result, and expanded the literature on neuro symbolic and expert network imaging.

Prepared the release, the code, the trained weights, the result file of every scored run and one driver per table and per figure, with a manifest that maps every quoted number to the script that produced it. We will release it after the paper is accepted, under a permanent citable identifier.

Read the objective line by line against the training code and corrected three statements it did not support. The clinical term runs over nine quantities as a weighted one sided penalty against a target taken from the backbone, the edge term is weighted toward the clean edges and carries three parts, and a sixth term of bounds and background protection that was active in training is now printed. Ten weight flags are parsed and never used, not three.
